segments.narration: People in a Kazakh village kept falling asleep for days mid-sentence. Starting in 2013, residents of Kalachi would black out without warning. They woke up days later with zero memory of what happened.
Animals were affected too. Cats hallucinated and dogs collapsed mid-bark. Doctors checked for viruses, radiation, and contaminated water, but every single test came back completely normal.
segments.visual_query: vintage hospital hallway medical lab equipment

segments.narration: Could an invisible threat be wiping out a town's consciousness? By 2015, over a hundred people had fallen victim to the sudden sleeping fits, turning Kalachi into a ghost town.
segments.visual_query: empty quiet streets remote kazakhstan town

segments.narration: The answer lay underground in an abandoned Soviet uranium mine. During specific weather shifts, high levels of carbon monoxide seeped into the valley, suffocating the town without them noticing.
The odorless gas displaced oxygen in the air, essentially forcing human brains into survival hibernation before anyone could smell a thing.
segments.visual_query: steam rising over snowy kazakhstan landscape

verdicts.claim: In 2013, residents of Kalachi, Kazakhstan began mysteriously falling asleep for days at a time.
verdicts.note: The reference article states that the sleeping sickness in Kalachi was first reported in March 2013 and caused people to sleep for days or weeks at a time with memory loss.

verdicts.claim: Medical tests ruled out radiation, heavy metals, and viral infections in Kalachi.
verdicts.note: The reference articles do not mention animals being affected or specific medical tests ruling out viruses, radiation, or heavy metals.

verdicts.claim: By 2015, over 100 residents in Kalachi had experienced the unexplained sleeping episodes.
verdicts.note: The reference text confirms the condition re-emerged in 2015 and had affected about 150 people by 2016.

verdicts.claim: An abandoned Soviet uranium mine near Kalachi was releasing elevated levels of carbon monoxide.
verdicts.note: The reference text states Kazakh officials concluded heightened levels of carbon monoxide from a nearby abandoned Soviet-era uranium mine caused the syndrome.

verdicts.claim: Carbon monoxide accumulation displaced oxygen and forced the brain into unconsciousness.
verdicts.note: The reference text notes that elevated carbon monoxide concentrations and reduced oxygen in the air were concluded to be the cause of the sleeping sickness.
